outcome.technical: tests/test_build_shop.py. (1) GROWTH OVER THE WHOLE SPAN: span_growth(lengths, secs) (line ~1918) returns time at the longest over time at the shortest and (length ratio in characters) ** TRIPWIRE_POWER; timing_faults judges grew > bound once per run and reports least room (bound/grew); tripwire_runs records each run's input lengths. TRIPWIRE_UNITS = (200, 51200) (was 200, 400, 800), TRIPWIRE_POWER unmoved at 1.5. Derivation written above the constant, from the wide measurement of 2026-11-20 (windows-2025 and ubuntu-24.04, python 3.12/3.14, two runs a job): over 200->51200 units the length ratio is 244-334 by kind, bound 3803-6108, largest time ratio 1978 (kind 2, bound 6108), LEAST ROOM 2.87 (windows python 3.14.10 run 1, processor time, a single quote left unpaired) over every file, run, kind and reading incl. node (node's least 14.9); ending at 25600 units the least room is 1.94 (< 2), so 51200 is the shortest end that holds; a quadratic reads L^2 = 59k-112k, 15.6-18.3x its bound. Two lengths only: the judgement reads the ends, a middle length would be judged by nothing and cost a series per kind and twin. (2) CEILING re-derived: TRIPWIRE_CEILING 0.25 -> 1.0 s. Longest text 1883359 characters (command substitutions + twin) x highest cost per character any reading showed, 142.5 ns (windows python 3.12.10) = 0.27 s idle; the red CI run read its longest at 800 units 2.35x the idle figure (0.0055 vs 0.00234 s, measured once) -> ~0.63 s loaded; 1.0 leaves 1.6 over that. (3) DEADLINES unmoved (TRIPWIRE_DEADLINE 10, TRIPWIRE_SERIES_DEADLINE 8): the new series costs at most 2.19 s a child on the 1/64 s clock at the windows numbers (31.8 s for every kind and twin), against 2.58 s / 40.7 s for the old three lengths (scratch sg2.11/cost.py), so nothing requires a raise. (4) EXITED CHILD: run_timers split into start_timers + collect_timers + child_output; child_output reads a child whose communicate timed out but which has exited (poll() not None) and kills only one still running; one deadline from the common start (each child's own, since they start together). Confirmed on this host that communicate(timeout=0) raises TimeoutExpired for an exited child on posix too. (5) NEW CASES: esc66 windows history (WINDOWS_UNITS 200/400/800/51200, WINDOWS_SECONDS, measured 2026-11-20 windows-2025 python 3.14.10 run 1, processor time) within the bound over the span in every kind (least room 2.87) while per doubling it reads up to 4.16x > 2.83, and the recorded lengths still equal the texts the suite builds; esc67 the same costs driven through _harness.growth_series by a substituted engine on a virtual clock stepping 1/64 s (virtual_series): green, least room 2.86, at most 2.17 s a child, 31.8 s for all, within TRIPWIRE_SERIES_DEADLINE; esc68 a quadratic cost on the same clock with no deadline fails the judgement in every kind; esc69 a slow child (sleeping EXITED_SLOW_SLEEP) and a fast one collected after the deadline: slow killed, fast read with its answer, not killed - no engine needed. esc53/esc55 wording now names the whole-span judgement and least room; the timing pass prints each engine's slowest child read time against TRIPWIRE_DEADLINE. (6) CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]: the sentence saying the suite times at lengths 'each double the last' against TRIPWIRE_POWER was false after this change; rewritten to the whole-span judgement and the exited-child reading. CHANGELOG.md is outside the task's files; the plan gate allowed the edit. Suite: 72 -> 76 cases.
